children.text: Throughout the entire video, Noel relies on key platform affordances, using clean visual editing and concise onscreen text overlays to emphasize his most important words. By maintaining a simple setup with no distracting objects in the background, just a direct-to-camera shot without any flashy edits or aggressive sales plugs, he leverages Instagram’s video format to create an authentic, face-to-face atmosphere, making the viewer feel more welcome. This deliberate visual restraint prevents the video from feeling commercialized and fake, allowing the serious mood of Men’s Mental Health Month to take center stage. The minimalistic production style strengthens his emotional appeal by making the interaction feel like an honest, personal conversation, such as one you would have with a friend.

Noel opens the video with a serious tone, talking about how he almost ended his life when he was in his 20s. Through the affordance of the text caption, “I nearly offed myself” can be seen, which carries a certain weight and disturbance with it. The fact that the word “killed,” and that Noel must mold his sentence to avoid directly saying that he almost committed suicide are just two sick examples of the language constraint that is enforced by Instagram. To bypass getting shadow banned or having his content removed due to platform guidelines, he adopts filtered internet slang while still maintaining his emotional vulnerability to build immediate rapport with his followers and any new viewers that may come along.
